arena: Classic Generic procedural_v2 11x9 two-player, action limit1000, reply-search self-play root256/slate8/opponent64, rounds divisible by eight
verification: Each exported opponent action was replayed from its exact preceding state, mapped to a legal action index, and the complete replay matched the native searched reply game. Opt-in and default schemas, deterministic replay, Python loader alignment, 346 Python tests, Ruff, Rust CLI tests and Clippy -D warnings passed on SSH server.
interpretation: The frozen source policy often ranks the searched opponent's first action highly, but matches fewer than one fifth of entire teacher-forced reply plans. Agreement is weaker for Move and Build decisions than for EndTurn; among 44 beneficial nonstatic root candidates only one full searched reply plan is matched. These candidate plans are correlated within just 16 maps, and teacher-forced later states would not be visited after an autonomous policy mismatch. This is a structural action-imitation diagnostic, not a full-game policy comparison, causal explanation, or Elo. No neural student was trained, rated, or deployed.
next_step: On new disjoint fit/calibration/validation map windows, test whether supervised imitation of searched opponent decisions improves held-out whole-plan teacher-forced agreement and then autonomous response consequences. Keep this 16-map diagnostic window out of training and validation. Promote only after fresh complete both-seat independent-map games and runtime/profile gates.
